questions.stem: What does the prime cost in a manufacturing account include?

options.text: Direct materials, direct labor, and direct expenses
Indirect materials, indirect labor, and overheads

questions.explanation: Prime cost comprises direct materials, direct labor, and direct expenses, which are directly attributable to the production process.

distractorRationale.b: Indirect costs are part of factory overheads, not prime cost.
distractorRationale.c: Prime cost includes more than just materials and overheads.
distractorRationale.d: It includes direct materials as well.

questions.stem: Why is it important to adjust for work in progress in a manufacturing account?

options.text: To ensure accurate calculation of factory overheads
To reflect the actual cost of goods manufactured
To calculate the selling price of goods
To determine the total sales revenue

questions.explanation: Adjusting for work in progress ensures that the manufacturing account accurately reflects the cost of goods manufactured.

distractorRationale.a: Factory overheads are calculated separately from work in progress adjustments.
distractorRationale.c: Selling price is determined after calculating the cost of goods manufactured.
distractorRationale.d: Sales revenue is not directly related to work in progress adjustments.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT included in factory overheads?
questions.explanation: Direct labor is part of the prime cost, not factory overheads.

distractorRationale.a: Utilities are an indirect cost and part of factory overheads.
distractorRationale.c: Depreciation is an indirect cost included in factory overheads.
distractorRationale.d: Indirect materials are part of factory overheads.
